name: WE Energies

profile.address: Pewaukee Data Center, W237N1500, Busse Road, RidgeView Corporate Park, City of Pewaukee, Waukesha County, Wisconsin, 53188
profile.reading:
In the RidgeView Corporate Park business park in the City of Pewaukee, Waukesha County, Wisconsin, We Energies operates a facility identified as the Pewaukee Data Center at W237N1500 Busse Road. We Energies is the trade name of Wisconsin Electric Power Company, one of the two principal utility subsidiaries of Milwaukee based WEC Energy Group, and it is one of the larger investor owned utilities in the Upper Midwest, serving more than 1.1 million electric customers and roughly the same number of natural gas customers across Wisconsin, plus electric service in Michigan's Upper Peninsula and steam service to downtown Milwaukee.

A utility of that size runs a substantial amount of internal computing infrastructure that rarely gets public attention because none of it is offered commercially. Grid operations alone require systems for supervisory control and data acquisition, outage management, and increasingly for the kind of real time monitoring that smart meters and distribution automation depend on. On top of that sits the ordinary corporate technology load of a company with over a million customer accounts: billing systems, customer information systems, and the back office applications any utility of this scale needs to run continuously. Pewaukee, a western Milwaukee suburb with easy highway access via I-94, is a plausible and unremarkable location for a utility to place enterprise IT capacity, whether as a primary site or as a backup facility for its core operations closer to downtown Milwaukee.

We Energies has not published a page describing this specific building, its square footage, its power capacity, or what systems it houses, and no news coverage identifying it as a named, standalone facility has surfaced. That is ordinary for a utility's internal data center. Unlike a colocation provider, We Energies has no commercial reason to publish capacity or design details for a building that exists purely to support the company's own grid operations and back office systems, and utilities generally treat the physical security and specifications of facilities tied to grid control functions as sensitive rather than promotional information. What can be said with confidence is the location, the parent company, and the type of institution behind it. Beyond that, the building's role in We Energies' broader operations, and any details about its scale, remain undisclosed.
